title: Indicator lag at or above the turn length makes every label take another speaker's name with default thresholds; the manifest claims 1-3 s skew is tolerated
area: packages/core/src/domain/speaker-tile-alignment.ts (per-label share over whole turns, no settling window); manifest assumption 3 and Evidence 'lag 1-3 s'
evidence: Two speakers alternating strictly, turns of 4 s, indicator sampled 1 Hz and lagging speech by 3 s: both labels are named, each with the OTHER speaker's name (10/10 label decisions wrong over 5 seeded meetings; same at turn 3/lag 3, turn 5/lag 5, turn 6/lag 5, turn 10/lag 10). Four speakers round-robin, 6 s turns, lag 5 s: all four labels named with the previous speaker's name. Share of the wrong name per label is 75-83%, runner-up 17-25% falling under maxRunnerUpFraction 0.2. Randomised sweep (400 meetings, lag 0-5 s, mean turn 3-28 s, 2-4 speakers): 4 wrong of 703 named, all with mean turn under 5 s and lag over 3.5 s.
fix_direction: Make the evidence lag-robust: ignore the first settleSec (default >= maxLagSec, e.g. 5 s) of each turn and drop turns shorter than 2x that from the evidence, or require the winning name to hold in the second half of its turns; state the tolerated lag as a function of turn length in the manifest and correct the '1-3 s tolerated' claim. Regression: the lag grid above must give zero wrong names (refusals are fine).
verified_evidence: cycle 1 (commit 56fad7e): the recorded reproductions (2 speakers turn/lag 4/3, 3/3, 5/5, 6/5, 10/10; 4 speakers 6 s/5 s) re-run verbatim x20 meetings each plus 12 neighbouring cells: 0 named in 800 labels, 0 wrong (lag-unstable or timeline-misaligned); own oracle simulation 12,000 in-range meetings (seeds 100000-105999, 300000-305999) plus 4,000 at lag 5.5-6: 3 non-lag wrongs on the first generator (merged label on a truncated log x2, noise-dominated 26 s label x1), 0 on the corrected one

title: Conflicting observations at the same tSec are resolved by sorting on name: the alphabetically LAST name silently wins, and a name beats a null (release) at the same instant
area: packages/core/src/domain/speaker-tile-alignment.ts obs.sort tie-break and hold construction (to > ob.t)
evidence: log = for t in 0..59: {tSec:t,'Anna'} and {tSec:t,'Zed'}; one label spoken 0-60 -> named 'Zed', candidates [{Zed,60}], no trace of Anna and no conflict signal. With {tSec:t,'Anna'} plus {tSec:t,null} the name wins. A capture that reports several highlighted participants per sample (multi-speaker highlight, crosstalk) therefore attributes the label to whoever sorts last, and the real speaker's label gets the wrong name at 100% share.
fix_direction: Treat two different non-null names (or a name and a release) at the same tSec as a conflict: a release for that instant (or an explicit ambiguous error code), never an arbitrary winner. Regression: the two inputs above must not name the label.
verified_evidence: cycle 1: Anna+Zed at each of 60 s and Anna+null: label refused no-observations, 60 conflict instants; three names, same name twice, permutation of 20 random orders, 1 ms apart (not a conflict, later wins, order-free) all as specified
